source_context_translations.translation: Nameless, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; named, it is the mother of the ten thousand things.
Therefore, always without desire, one observes its mystery,
always with desire, one observes its boundary;
These two, the same in source but different in name, are both called the mysterious.
When all under heaven know beauty as beauty, then ugliness already exists.
He carries out a teaching without words; the myriad things arise, but he does not refuse them; he gives life to them but does not possess them; he acts on them but does not rely on them,
Because he does not dwell on them, they do not leave him.
Do not exalt the worthy, and the people will not contend; do not prize rare goods, and the people will not steal; do not display what can be desired, and the people’s minds will not be confused.
This makes the wise dare not act.

The Way is empty, yet in use it is never exhausted; deep and still, it seems to be the ancestor of the myriad things. It blunts its sharpness, unties its tangles, softens its light, and makes itself like dust; deep and still, it seems somehow to remain.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To own, hold, or be in possession of something.
additional_senses.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): The king has jade.
Though he is poor, he still has a surplus.
The gentleman has virtue.
There are books in the room.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): An existential verb introducing the presence or existence of something.
additional_senses.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): There are changes in the seasons.
Someone has come to the courtyard.
There is a spring below the mountain.
There are carts on the road ahead.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To exist, be present, or possess something; also used predicatively to state that something exists or is available.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often contrasts with 無 in the text’s philosophical vocabulary.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a reason or result, especially in a causative or purposive relationship.
additional_senses.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): Because the weather is cold, clothing is thick in order to ward it off.
The people are troubled, so the ruler reduces taxes to calm them.
Because the rain is heavy, the boat proceeds slowly.
The opportunity must not be lost, so he departs quickly to meet it.
Sentences: 時不可失，故速發以應之。

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Links one clause or phrase to the next, often with a sequential or instrumental sense.
additional_senses.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): First set oneself right, and then govern one’s family.
Remove profit and end contention, and then secure the state.
Nourish the breath and keep still, and then await the proper time.
Cultivate virtue and practice righteousness, and thereby move the people.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks the means, method, or purpose with which an action is done; here it introduces the way of contemplating.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Can link an action to its means or to its intended result.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
contextual_sense.Translation (English): by means of; in order to

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A border area or frontier region at the edge of a territory.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a frontier to the north.
An official guarding the border has arrived.
He crossed the border and entered.
The frontier is without alarm.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): As a verb, to pursue, seek, or head toward something.
Sentence Translations (English): The aspirant seeks profit.
The crowd pursues fame.
Do not seek favor from others.
Those far away head toward the near.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The observable boundary, surface, or outward aspect of something, especially what can be seen from the outside.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In the Laozi it often contrasts with deeper, hidden reality.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Forms a noun phrase from a verb, adjective, or clause, referring to the action, state, or thing described.
Sentence Translations (English): The wise are not perplexed.
The good can endure long.
One who speaks is without blame.
One who acts can go far.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person characterized by a certain quality or belonging to a certain group.
Sentence Translations (English): The brave are first to climb up.
The worthy dwell above.
The old are made secure.
The foolish are often suspicious.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A noun marker referring to persons or things previously identified, often meaning 'those who' or 'the ones that.'
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Functions to turn a preceding description into a referential noun phrase.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A feeling of aversion toward someone or something.
additional_senses.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone hates disorder.
The people dislike his violence.
I do not dislike you.
The gentleman does not resent another’s goodness.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To speak against someone in a way that harms their reputation.
Sentence Translations (English): Do not slander his name.
The petty man likes to slander the worthy.
Many mouths can defame a person.
Do not defame him out of private resentment.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Morally or aesthetically bad, undesirable, or opposite to what is judged good or beautiful.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage, the sense is shaped by contrast with 美 and points to the opposite pole of valuation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To excuse oneself from accepting or performing something; to decline politely or formally.
Sentence Translations (English): The king declined it.
Your servant dares not refuse.
He then declined the rank.
Everyone was willing to go, but I alone refused.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Words used in parting, or the act of taking leave from someone.
Sentence Translations (English): At departure he delivered a farewell.
They composed parting words together.
The guest is about to leave; please make a farewell verse.
At midnight he took leave and departed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Words given as a response, explanation, or excuse; also speech or verbal utterance in general.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is negated to mean that things arise without verbal reply or explanation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): An adult male person, especially a husband or man in a general sense.
Sentence Translations (English): Husband and wife respect one another.
Her husband died early.
One man guards the gate.
This old man asks to go.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A demonstrative or topical particle used to point to or take up something previously mentioned.
Sentence Translations (English): The Way is utterly simple.
As for the nature of the people.
Weapons of war are ominous implements.
Only when one knows to stop does it work.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A sentence-initial particle or discourse marker, often introducing a topic, emphasis, or exclamatory turn of thought.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text it adds a meditative, expository tone rather than lexical meaning.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
contextual_sense.Translation (English): the latter part of the sentence marker; intensive particle

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To come into contact with someone or something, especially by meeting face to face or coming upon it.
Sentence Translations (English): He met a guest at dawn.
He met a friend on the road.
Suddenly he encountered a person.
After a long separation they met again.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To appear before a superior or to receive someone formally.
Sentence Translations (English): Your servant requests an audience.
The envoy seeks an audience.
Tomorrow he will meet the king.
The guest is granted an audience with his lord.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To visually perceive or become aware of something; also to let something be seen.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this passage, it governs 可欲 and means ‘display’ or ‘set before the eyes.’
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The common people as a collective social body.
additional_senses.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): Love the people as if they were your children.
When the ruler loses the Way, the people’s hearts depart.
One who calms the people wins the realm.
Benevolent government lies in harmonizing the people’s hearts.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The collective feelings, loyalties, and attitudes of the populace.
additional_senses.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
Sentence Translations (English): Highest virtue harmonizes public sentiment.
Severe punishments make the people resentful.
One who wins the people’s hearts prospers.
One who loses the people’s hearts perishes.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The inner faculty of thought, feeling, intention, and awareness regarded as a single whole.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In early Chinese thought this is not just intellect but the integrated inner state of a person.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): People distinguished by wisdom or good judgment as a class.
Sentence Translations (English): The wise are not perplexed.
The wise discern what is near at hand.
The wise speak cautiously.
The wise can make decisions.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Someone who relies on intellect, wit, or strategy, especially in practical affairs.
Sentence Translations (English): A calculating person has many schemes.
The crowd fears clever men.
Do not let clever men monopolize power.
He is not a warrior, but only a clever man.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A person regarded as intelligent, discerning, or wise; often one who has special knowledge or practical insight.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it refers to those with intelligence or cleverness, not necessarily moral sagehood.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To fill up or occupy completely, especially a vessel or space.
Sentence Translations (English): The water seeks to fill the vessel.
If it is not full, it is hard to fill it.
The vessel is already filled.
Be careful not to overfill the cup.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To drive forward against something with force, or to collide with it.
Sentence Translations (English): The cart rushed against the gate.
The horse charged the battle line.
The boat struck the bank.
Anger surged against the man.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Being hollow, empty, or not full; lacking solid contents, with stress on internal openness.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In the Laozi, this physical emptiness is also valued as functional openness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): received Classical Chinese; Laozi/Wang Bi recension
